# qBittorrent

qBittorrent is the download client. Mediaplane runs the upstream LinuxServer.io image,
unmodified, and by default puts it behind Gluetun's VPN.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by "pnpm docs:generate" from app.ts. Do not edit. -->

## What Mediaplane sets

- **Image:** `lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:5.2.4_v2.0.15-ls479`
- **Digest:** `sha256:b522f9f4b769f8f36d49d22d5eb6a92e9aa18904c6a1830b1439df511ec21983`
- **Architectures:** amd64, arm64
- **Ports:** 8080/tcp (web), published as `network.bind` says; `apps.qbittorrent.port` moves the host and container port together (`WEBUI_PORT`)
- **Volumes:** `<home>/appdata/qbittorrent` → `/config`; the data folder (`paths.data`) → `/data`
- **Runs as:** the stack's `user:`, through `PUID` and `PGID`
- **Health check:** `curl -fsS "http://localhost:${WEBUI_PORT}/" > /dev/null`, every 30s (timeout 10s, 5 retries, 60s to start)
- **Secrets:** `apiKey`: `qbt_` and 28 random letters and digits, generated once and kept in `state/secrets.json`
- **API:** on its `web` port, which Mediaplane reaches over the stack's wiring network, with `apiKey` as a Bearer token
- **Managed in the app:** `qbittorrent.admin`: fields `qbittorrent.admin.username` (fixed); the secret `password`, checked and never shown. `qbittorrent.preferences`: fields `qbittorrent.preferences.savePath`, `qbittorrent.preferences.autoTmm`, `qbittorrent.preferences.authSubnetWhitelistEnabled` (fixed), `qbittorrent.preferences.authSubnetWhitelist` (fixed). `qbittorrent.category_tv`: fields `qbittorrent.category_tv.savePath`. `qbittorrent.category_movies`: fields `qbittorrent.category_movies.savePath`
- **Needs:** nothing
- **Provides:** `download-client:torrent`
- **Also turns on:** `gluetun`, with the default settings

<!-- END GENERATED -->

## What Mediaplane does today

- **Behind the VPN** (`apps.qbittorrent.vpn: true`, the default):
  - qBittorrent uses Gluetun's network (`network_mode: service:gluetun`), so its traffic
    leaves through Gluetun's VPN tunnel and firewall;
  - it starts only once Gluetun is healthy, and Compose restarts it when it recreates
    Gluetun. When Gluetun has started again without it, by hand or after a crash, or
    when `apply` starts a stopped Gluetun, `apply` restarts qBittorrent too, so that it
    joins Gluetun's new network: `plan` lists it as `restart`;
  - its web UI is published on Gluetun's service;
  - `stack.yaml` needs a `vpn:` block, or `plan` reports an error;
  - an end-to-end test checks that it has no way out when the VPN is down, against a
    WireGuard server of its own, and `mediaplane vpn-check` checks the same on your host
    (see [Gluetun's README](../gluetun/README.md)). vpn-check runs its probe in
    qBittorrent's own image, as nobody: a throwaway container that writes nothing.
- **Without the VPN** (`vpn: false`), it has its own network, and `plan` warns every time.
- **Its API, over the wiring network.** `plan` and `apply` check that Mediaplane's key
  still opens qBittorrent's API, sent as a Bearer token. Behind the VPN they reach it
  through Gluetun, which is on the stack's wiring network for it, at qBittorrent's own
  port. Through that API, once qBittorrent runs, `apply` manages:
  - **the shared admin login** (`qbittorrent.admin`): its user name, and its password,
    checked by signing in, and set with the key when it differs. So a change of
    `admin.username` or `admin.password` reaches qBittorrent, with no restart;
  - **its settings** (`qbittorrent.preferences`): the default save path
    `/data/torrents`, Automatic Torrent Management on, and who may skip the login: your
    LAN subnets, only with `security.login_on_lan: false` and the web UI published on
    your LAN, as the file below sets them;
  - **a category for each arr in the stack** (`qbittorrent.category_tv` with Sonarr,
    `qbittorrent.category_movies` with Radarr), saving to `/data/torrents/tv` and
    `/data/torrents/movies`. With Automatic Torrent Management, a torrent goes to its
    category's folder.
- **Sonarr's and Radarr's download client.** Sonarr and Radarr reach qBittorrent as
  `gluetun` behind the VPN (`qbittorrent` without it), at qBittorrent's own port, with
  its key. Gluetun counts the stack's networks as local, so its firewall lets them in:
  an end-to-end test (`test/e2e/download.e2e.test.ts`) runs their own test of it. See
  [Sonarr's README](../sonarr/README.md).
- **One port, inside and out.** qBittorrent checks the `Host` header, so the published
  port and its own port must match. `apps.qbittorrent.port` changes both, through
  `WEBUI_PORT`, and `apps.qbittorrent.env` refuses `WEBUI_PORT`.
- **`qBittorrent.conf`, before its first start.** Mediaplane writes
  `appdata/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/qBittorrent.conf`, only if it doesn't exist, with:
  - **the shared admin login:** the user name, and a PBKDF2 hash of the password, never
    the password itself. `mediaplane credentials` shows the login;
  - **its API key** (`WebUI\APIKey`), generated once and kept in `state/secrets.json`.
    Sonarr and Radarr use it too;
  - **the save path** `/data/torrents/`;
  - **Automatic Torrent Management on,** so a torrent follows its category's save path.
    That includes torrents you add by hand;
  - **UPnP off,** so nothing opens a port on your router;
  - **a login on localhost too** (`WebUI\LocalHostAuth`);
  - **your LAN without a login** (`WebUI\AuthSubnetWhitelist`), only with
    `security.login_on_lan: false` and the web UI published on your LAN. It lists your LAN
    subnets, separated by commas. If Mediaplane knows no LAN subnet, `plan` warns
    (`network.no-lan-subnet`).

  qBittorrent keeps these and adds its own settings, and starts with no temporary
  password. Mediaplane never changes the file after that: from then on, it manages the
  login and the settings above through qBittorrent's API, and the rest are yours to
  change in qBittorrent's web UI.

## Drift and Keep mine

- **What drift reports.** `mediaplane drift`, and `plan`, report a change made in
  qBittorrent's web UI to what Mediaplane manages here, listed above under "Managed in the
  app": what Mediaplane set, and what qBittorrent holds now. A secret is checked with
  qBittorrent's own test, and named, never shown. `apply` puts each back.
- **Keeping yours.** `mediaplane keep qbittorrent.<resource>.<field>`, as drift names it,
  keeps what qBittorrent holds instead: it adds the line under `overrides:` in `stack.yaml`,
  and `apply` then leaves it. A field marked `(fixed)` above, and a secret, can't be
  kept. `mediaplane keep qbittorrent.category_movies` stops Mediaplane managing a
  resource deleted in qBittorrent. The
  [drift runbook](../../docs/runbooks/drift-reported.md) says more.
- **Its admin user name and who may skip its login** are fixed: the user name is the
  shared admin login (change `admin.username` in `stack.yaml`), and the whitelist is a
  security setting (set `security.login_on_lan`). Drift still reports a change to
  either, and `apply` puts it back.
- **Its password, changed in qBittorrent,** is checked by signing in, once per `plan`.
  Once drift has found it refused, neither drift nor `plan` signs in again until `apply`
  sets it, which spares Mediaplane the ban below.
- **Its key, changed in qBittorrent,** reads as `qbittorrent: refuses the key Mediaplane
holds for it`. Neither drift nor `plan` sends that key again until `apply` checks it,
  as each refusal may count towards the ban below. Put the stored key back, as the
  [wiring failed runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md#fix) shows, then run
  `apply`.
- **A download client's category, kept as another**
  (`mediaplane keep sonarr.download_client.category`), becomes this category's name too:
  the category `qbittorrent.category_tv` makes is then the kept one, with its save path
  under `/data/torrents`, and `apply` makes it. Until it does, drift leaves Sonarr's
  client's key unchecked, saying `apply` puts what it requires in place first. The
  category made before stays, yours. A kept category must stay a folder in
  `/data/torrents`: a folder name, or several joined by `/` (a subcategory such as
  `tv/anime`), never empty, nor with a `.` or `..` folder, a `/` at either end or two
  together, a `\`, or a control character. `keep` and `plan` refuse one that isn't.
- **A category you stop Mediaplane managing** (`qbittorrent.category_tv: unmanaged`, or
  `_movies`) is yours, and stays the category Sonarr's or Radarr's download client files
  under: while qBittorrent lacks it, `plan` and drift leave that client's key unchecked,
  as the arr's own test would make it, with no save path. To clear it, make the category
  in qBittorrent, or name one in the arr that qBittorrent has (and keep that), then run
  drift again.

## Changing it

- **In `stack.yaml`,** under `apps.qbittorrent`, you can set `vpn`, `port`, `version`,
  `env` and `enabled: false`. A different `version` is an untested combination, and
  `plan` warns about it. See the
  [`stack.yaml` reference](../../docs/reference/stack-yaml.md).
- **Anything else** goes in `compose.override.yaml` in the Mediaplane home. Behind the
  VPN, qBittorrent has no network of its own, so ports and network settings belong on
  `gluetun`, not here.

## Known issues

- **After Gluetun restarts on its own, qBittorrent has no network** until it restarts
  too. `mediaplane vpn-check` reports it, and `mediaplane apply` restarts qBittorrent;
  see [Gluetun's README](../gluetun/README.md).
- **A change made in qBittorrent's web UI to what Mediaplane manages is undone** by the
  next `apply`: the login, the save path, Automatic Torrent Management, who may skip the
  login, and the two categories' save paths. `plan` and `mediaplane drift` show it first,
  and `mediaplane keep` keeps it instead (see above).
- **Five failed sign-ins in a row ban an address for an hour.** Mediaplane checks the
  password by signing in, once per `plan` and once per `apply`, and never again after a
  timeout. So after you change `admin.password`, run `apply` soon: four `plan`s, or
  declined `apply`s, are enough to get Mediaplane's address banned (never your browser's),
  and `plan` then says so. Restarting qBittorrent lifts the ban. See the
  [wiring failed runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md).
- **A `network.lan_subnet` wider than your LAN lets everything in it skip the login,**
  with `security.login_on_lan: false` and the web UIs published on your LAN
  (`network.bind` is not `localhost`). An address inside the whitelisted subnet signs in
  with any password. If the subnet also covers a Docker network of the stack, such as a
  hand-typed `172.16.0.0/12`, which covers Docker's `172.17` to `172.31` networks:
  - every container on those networks skips qBittorrent's login;
  - `plan` can't see a password changed by hand in qBittorrent, because its check signs
    in from the wiring network.

  Set `network.lan_subnet` to your LAN itself, such as `192.168.1.0/24`.

- **Removing `admin.password`** brings back the password Mediaplane generated before, if
  it generated one: it keeps it, and never generates another. `apply` then sets it in
  qBittorrent.
- **Set up before Slice 3a.** If qBittorrent first started before Mediaplane wrote its
  `qBittorrent.conf`, its file has no API key. `plan` lists `qbittorrent.apiKey` under
  `Keys to put back in their apps' own files`: `apply` stops qBittorrent, puts the key in
  its file, under `[Preferences]`, keeping the rest, and starts it again. The file's
  login is still the image's, with its temporary password: the wiring then sets the
  shared login, through the key.
- **Its key made anew in its web UI** (Options, WebUI, API key) is written into
  `qBittorrent.conf` at once, and shuts Mediaplane out. `apply` puts the stored key back,
  restarting qBittorrent; or `mediaplane keep qbittorrent.apiKey` keeps the new one, and
  the next `apply` gives it to Sonarr's and Radarr's download clients. The
  [rebuilding a host runbook](../../docs/runbooks/rebuilding-a-host.md#a-key-changed-at-its-source)
  has the details.
- **Its key after a lost `state/`** is read back from `qBittorrent.conf`, before anything
  is generated. One Mediaplane can't read stops `plan` (`keys.unrecoverable`).
